description: While the restored copy runs, starting the original client directory fails only because the saved port is taken: "PORT_IN_USE: Port 54113 is in use by another process; choose another --http-port". Following that advice starts a second active copy of the same identity and device. Both connect to the Harbor Infra hub, and both serve the Billing Alerts hub, which the recovery doc explicitly forbids. Nothing detects the duplicate.
expected: Detect a duplicate device identity (at the hub, or locally through a per-device marker or lease) and refuse with "This client was restored elsewhere; only one active copy may run." At the very least, the PORT_IN_USE message should not suggest --http-port when the port belongs to another Pardner client with the same identity.
actual: The second copy runs and connects.
suggested_fix: Have the hub reject a second concurrent replica connection for the same device and replica ID. Have the port probe identify the occupant as the same Pardner identity and say so.

description: Cold backup and restore depend on hand-typed shell (`umask 077`, `test ! -e`, `cp -Rp`) taken from the docs. There is no `client backup` or `client restore` command that checks the service is stopped, preserves modes and refuses overwrites.
expected: `pardner client backup --output DIR` (refusing when running or when DIR exists) and a matching restore check.
suggested_fix: Wrap the documented procedure in a CLI command.

description: With the local service stopped, the board keeps New task enabled, and the restored board shows a stale presence dot on a card from the pre-backup session.
expected: Mutating entry points are disabled while the local service is unreachable, as they are while a request is pending.
actual: New task is enabled during the outage.
suggested_fix: Gate New task on the connection state as well as on pending.
